hook: A very short file about an unfinished, handwritten piece of music dug out of a tomb. Content note: it describes self-harm and suicide, though in brief, clinical language. Read the procedures closely, since they quietly tell you what the object does before the description does.
whyItMatters: It is a compact cognitohazard story: one idea, a composition that drives anyone who sees it to try to complete it, carried by a handful of paragraphs. The score's title, On Mount Golgotha, also appears as a tag on the page. It shows how much menace a short entry can hold when procedures and description reinforce each other.
thingsToNotice:
The containment rules tell the story in reverse: darkness, an iron box and suspension well away from the walls all make sense once you learn what seeing the score does.

The ink turns out to be blood from several people, which recasts the sheet as something built out of earlier victims. Everyone exposed does the same thing: they cut themselves open to write more of the piece in their own blood, and the few who finish a section kill themselves at once, saying it can never be completed. Two members of the salvage team that found it had already gone mad and bled themselves badly trying to finish it. The final line, that performing it yields only clashing noise with no harmony between parts, suggests the thing was never really music, and the religious title is left for the reader to interpret.
